whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Energy & Utilities Accredited Professional exam for?

personas.label: Utility industry implementation consultants
personas.description: You implement Salesforce for an electric, gas or water utility and work with customer and service data.

personas.label: Salesforce admins at utility companies
personas.description: You administer Energy & Utilities Cloud and need to understand premises, service points and utility workflows.

personas.label: OmniStudio and integration partners
personas.description: You build utility customer journeys or integrations with billing and meter systems.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Energy & Utilities Accredited Professional Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The exam covers utility workflows and the Energy & Utilities data model, including customer relationships, premises, service points, usage and integrations. Utility experience can help with industry terms.
bullets: 50 scored questions in 75 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
60% to pass, which is 30 correct answers out of 50.
Utility data model: Review how accounts, premises, service points, and meters relate.
OmniStudio and integrations: Practise identifying where guided scripts, FlexCards, and connections to billing systems fit.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Use practice tests to identify weak topics. Before booking, explain how accounts, premises, service points, and meters connect, and review a utility implementation or meter-to-cash process.

examFormat.heading: Energy & Utilities Accredited Professional Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or in person. Check the current exam guide for the latest requirements and delivery details.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Scenarios describe a customer or utility process. Identify the customer relationship, premise, service point and external system involved before selecting records or a workflow.
bestWayToPass: Learn how customer accounts, billing relationships, premises, service points and meters differ.
Review the OmniStudio journeys and service processes in the current product materials.
Understand where usage, billing and service data originate and how Salesforce integrates with those systems.
Use practice questions to find topics to revisit in Salesforce Help.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers the Energy & Utilities Cloud data model, customer journeys, outages and billing integrations. Review how premises, service points and meter-to-cash processes fit together.

keyConcepts.h2: Energy and Utilities Cloud: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Energy & Utilities Cloud Data Model
blocks.body: Energy & Utilities Cloud uses an industry data model to represent customers, billing relationships, premises, service points and equipment. A premise is the physical location. A service point is where a service is delivered to that premise; separate metered services can have separate service points. Accounts and billing accounts represent customer and payment relationships, while assets can represent installed meters or other equipment.

blocks.heading: OmniStudio-Powered Customer Journeys
blocks.body: OmniStudio can support utility service journeys. An OmniScript can guide a customer or agent through starting service, moving, or reporting an outage. FlexCards can show useful context such as account details, bills, and service orders. Practise adapting the supplied components to a utility’s business rules.

blocks.heading: Field Service Integration
blocks.body: A utility can use Field Service to plan and dispatch work such as meter installation, connection, or repair. Review how a service order relates to a work order and how scheduling assigns work to a crew. Mobile workers can receive jobs and record progress in the field.

blocks.heading: Customer Portal and Self-Service
blocks.body: An Experience Cloud site can give customers a place to view billing information, request service changes, or report an outage. Knowledge articles can answer common questions. Plan the site around the services available to customers and the utility’s access and validation requirements.

blocks.heading: Billing Integration and Account Management
blocks.body: A utility may keep billing in an external system such as SAP IS-U or Oracle CC&B while using Salesforce for customer engagement. Decide which balances, usage details, and service requests must move between systems, how often to sync them, and how to handle errors or conflicting updates.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Energy & Utilities Accredited Professional Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Identify the customer relationship, physical premise, service point and external system in each scenario.

blocks.heading: Separate place from customer
blocks.body: A premise is the physical location. Customer and billing relationships can change while the location remains.

blocks.heading: Read the service point carefully
blocks.body: A service point represents the entry for a service at a premise; separate metered services can have distinct points.

blocks.heading: Trace readings to their source
blocks.body: Check which system owns meter data and how Salesforce receives it before choosing an integration.

blocks.heading: Follow work into the field
blocks.body: Relate a utility service request to the appropriate field work records when a technician visit is needed.

sampleQuestions.question: How should a utility model a customer relationship, the service location and separately metered connections?
options: One account for the customer and the service location
Store the location as an account address
Create separate customer, premise and service-point records
Put meter details in a contact note
sampleQuestions.explanation: Create separate customer, premise and service-point records is the best fit because the customer or billing account represents the commercial relationship; the premise represents the location, and a service point represents an individually metered service connection. These are related records with separate roles.
whyWrong: One account for the customer and the service location is not the best choice because one account does not represent the separate physical location and service connections.
Store the location as an account address is not the best choice because address fields alone do not model the relationship between premises and service points.
Put meter details in a contact note is not the best choice because a note cannot represent a service connection as a structured record.

sampleQuestions.question: In the Energy & Utilities model, what does a service point identify?
options: A billing account for the customer
Metered connection at a premise
The premise address itself
A reading from a billing period
sampleQuestions.explanation: Metered connection at a premise is the best fit because a service point is the entry point for a service at a premise; separately metered services are represented by distinct service points.
whyWrong: A billing account for the customer is not the best choice because the billing account represents the customer’s payment relationship.
The premise address itself is not the best choice because the premise is the physical location, not a service point.
A reading from a billing period is not the best choice because a reading records usage at a service point; it is not the service connection.

sampleQuestions.question: When a new customer moves into an existing premise, which records and history should remain?
options: Replace the premise with a new customer account
Remove the service point and earlier readings
Leave the old customer responsible for the new occupant’s bill
Keep the premise and service history; update the customer and billing links
sampleQuestions.explanation: Keep the premise and service history; update the customer and billing links is the best fit because the premise remains the physical location, and the service point represents the service connection there. Move processes update the relevant customer and billing relationships while retaining service history.
whyWrong: Replace the premise with a new customer account is not the best choice because a customer move does not change the physical premise.
Remove the service point and earlier readings is not the best choice because deleting the service point would discard useful service and reading history.
Leave the old customer responsible for the new occupant’s bill is not the best choice because the previous customer should not be billed for the new occupant.

sampleQuestions.question: What can interval usage data show that a monthly total cannot?
options: Billing systems cannot accept a monthly total
Salesforce cannot store monthly usage without custom code
Regulators require every reading to be public within thirty days
Usage timing can affect tariffs and demand charges
sampleQuestions.explanation: Usage timing can affect tariffs and demand charges is the best fit because time-of-use tariffs and demand charges depend on when energy was used, which a single monthly total cannot express.
whyWrong: Billing systems cannot accept a monthly total is not the best choice because monthly totals are processable; they are just less useful.
Salesforce cannot store monthly usage without custom code is not the best choice because monthly totals are perfectly storable; the issue is what they can tell you.
Regulators require every reading to be public within thirty days is not the best choice because publication of individual readings is not a general requirement.

sampleQuestions.question: What should an agent review first when a customer disputes a meter reading?
options: Credit the full bill and close the case
Replace the meter before checking the complaint
Review the service point’s reading history
Move the customer to a cheaper tariff
sampleQuestions.explanation: Review the service point’s reading history is the best fit because the reading history shows whether the figure is consistent with past consumption, which is what tells you if there is a genuine problem.
whyWrong: Credit the full bill and close the case is not the best choice because crediting before investigating gives away revenue without establishing cause.
Replace the meter before checking the complaint is not the best choice because replacing hardware is expensive and premature before checking the data.
Move the customer to a cheaper tariff is not the best choice because changing tariff does not address whether the reading was correct.

sampleQuestions.question: What information does a usage profile provide?
options: The customer’s typical consumption pattern
A list of appliances at the premise
A credit score for payment plans
A record of the customer’s past complaints
sampleQuestions.explanation: The customer’s typical consumption pattern is the best fit because usage profiles describe expected consumption patterns, which support estimating, forecasting and spotting anomalies.
whyWrong: A list of appliances at the premise is not the best choice because appliance inventories are not what a usage profile is for.
A credit score for payment plans is not the best choice because credit assessment is a separate commercial process.
A record of the customer’s past complaints is not the best choice because complaint history is case management rather than usage.

sampleQuestions.question: How can one commercial agreement cover service at twelve locations?
options: One contract with twelve sites described in free text
Twelve contracts, one for each location
One contract associated with twelve service points
Twelve customer accounts with separate contract terms
sampleQuestions.explanation: One contract associated with twelve service points is the best fit because a contract can cover many service points, which is what lets a single commercial agreement span multiple sites.
whyWrong: One contract with twelve sites described in free text is not the best choice because addresses in free text cannot be billed or reported against.
Twelve contracts, one for each location is not the best choice because separate contracts per site lose the single commercial agreement.
Twelve customer accounts with separate contract terms is not the best choice because splitting the customer into twelve accounts fragments the relationship.

sampleQuestions.question: In a deregulated market, what choice may be available to the customer?
options: Whether a customer can choose a supplier
Whether Salesforce may store customer data
Whether the utility provides only electricity
Whether readings arrive monthly or quarterly
sampleQuestions.explanation: Whether a customer can choose a supplier is the best fit because deregulated markets let customers choose a retail supplier, which changes the processes a utility needs for switching and enrolment.
whyWrong: Whether Salesforce may store customer data is not the best choice because data residency is a separate legal question.
Whether the utility provides only electricity is not the best choice because the commodities supplied are unrelated to regulation.
Whether readings arrive monthly or quarterly is not the best choice because reading frequency is an operational choice, not the market structure.

sampleQuestions.question: Which plan can spread expected annual charges across twelve monthly payments?
options: A contract backdated to the financial year’s start
An extra service point for instalments
Monthly credits against actual use
A budget or levelised payment plan
sampleQuestions.explanation: A budget or levelised payment plan is the best fit because budget plans charge a level amount each month and reconcile against actual consumption periodically.
whyWrong: A contract backdated to the financial year’s start is not the best choice because backdating a contract does not change how the customer pays.
An extra service point for instalments is not the best choice because service points represent premises, not payment arrangements.
Monthly credits against actual use is not the best choice because monthly credit notes would misstate what the customer actually owes.

sampleQuestions.question: Why connect Salesforce to a meter data management system?
options: Store customer contact and marketing preferences
Manage validated meter readings
Generate every regulated customer invoice
Schedule field technicians and vehicles
sampleQuestions.explanation: Manage validated meter readings is the best fit because meter data management holds and validates the readings, so Salesforce consumes that data rather than owning it.
whyWrong: Store customer contact and marketing preferences is not the best choice because consent and preferences live with the customer record.
Generate every regulated customer invoice is not the best choice because invoicing is done by the billing system, not the meter data platform.
Schedule field technicians and vehicles is not the best choice because field resources are managed in field service.

sampleQuestions.question: How can an agent view a customer’s usage, billing details and cases together?
options: Agent console with customer context
A weekly email with every agent’s open customers and cases
A nightly spreadsheet extract agents can search
Separate browser tabs for each source system
sampleQuestions.explanation: Agent console with customer context is the best fit because a console layout surfaces related records in context, which is what lets an agent answer a question without leaving the record.
whyWrong: A weekly email with every agent’s open customers and cases is not the best choice because a weekly report is stale by the time a customer calls.
A nightly spreadsheet extract agents can search is not the best choice because a spreadsheet extract is neither current nor auditable.
Separate browser tabs for each source system is not the best choice because switching between systems slows every call and invites mistakes.

sampleQuestions.question: Why associate asset records with service points?
options: Track customer campaign responses
Record equipment installed at the premise
Store tariff rates for service points
Keep annual regulatory filings
sampleQuestions.explanation: Record equipment installed at the premise is the best fit because assets represent the physical equipment, such as meters, installed at a premise, which can be replaced while the premise stays the same.
whyWrong: Track customer campaign responses is not the best choice because campaign response belongs to marketing records.
Store tariff rates for service points is not the best choice because tariffs are commercial terms, not physical equipment.
Keep annual regulatory filings is not the best choice because regulatory filings are documents, not installed assets.

sampleQuestions.question: What is an efficient way to add service records for 400 new premises?
options: One service point for the entire development
Bulk-load the service-point records
Create each premise from an individual support case
Ask the meter system to create Salesforce records
sampleQuestions.explanation: Bulk-load the service-point records is the best fit because each premise needs its own service point, and 400 of them is a data load rather than a manual task.
whyWrong: One service point for the entire development is not the best choice because one service point cannot represent 400 separately billed premises.
Create each premise from an individual support case is not the best choice because manual creation of 400 records is slow and inconsistent.
Ask the meter system to create Salesforce records is not the best choice because the meter data system does not own the Salesforce service point records.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a utility work order normally describe?
options: The expected yearly usage pattern
A monthly energy invoice
A field job to be completed at a premise
The customer’s supply contract
sampleQuestions.explanation: A field job to be completed at a premise is the best fit because work orders capture jobs such as installations, reads and repairs, and link to the service point where the work happens.
whyWrong: The expected yearly usage pattern is not the best choice because expected consumption is a usage profile.
A monthly energy invoice is not the best choice because invoices are billing records.
The customer’s supply contract is not the best choice because contracts are commercial agreements.

sampleQuestions.question: Why keep premise records separate from the people who occupy them?
options: Premise history survives customer moves
Avoid connecting to the meter data system
Stop attaching tariffs to contracts
Reduce the number of records stored
sampleQuestions.explanation: Premise history survives customer moves is the best fit because supply history belongs to the address, and occupiers come and go, so separating them is what keeps consumption history intact across moves.
whyWrong: Avoid connecting to the meter data system is not the best choice because a meter-data integration may still be needed for readings and usage history.
Stop attaching tariffs to contracts is not the best choice because tariffs can still be associated with the applicable commercial terms.
Reduce the number of records stored is not the best choice because record count is not the reason to separate a place from its changing occupants.
